p01.why: A storage class must not be combined with typedef.

p02.why: The block static is initialized at the first call, so slots is 14 in any unit order, and the constinit variable is 64 before any code runs.

p03.why: b is destroyed before a, and each recursive call creates a new local object at a different address.

p04.why: The two inline definitions differ, which needs no diagnostic; each call returns 1 or 2 depending on the linker, and the program accepts either.

p05.why: Two units define the same non-inline variable, and the linker reports a multiple definition.

p06.why: thread_local combines with static and extern, the declarations of c agree, and in a block thread_local implies static; there is no main.

p08.why: A static data member cannot be mutable, and mutable with static is two storage classes.

p09.why: A reference member cannot be mutable.

p10.why: A function must not be declared thread_local.

p11.why: A static declaration follows a declaration with external linkage.

p12.why: c is initialized last, so the order of destruction is c, b, a, and the check in a's destructor passes.

p13.why: A block thread_local is initialized once in the thread at the first pass, so a is 2, b is 3, and make runs once.

p14.why: count was first declared with external linkage, so the later static definition is not valid.

p15.why: A mutable non-static data member can change through a const object, so hits becomes 1.

p16.why: main must not be declared static.

p17.why: Each function's local value hides the global one, so the three values are 1, 2, and 3.

p18.why: A const volatile variable keeps external linkage, so the definition in the second unit is the one the first unit reads.

p19.why: extern on the const definition gives it external linkage, so the first unit reads 42.

p20.why: The block extern redeclares the earlier static hidden and takes its internal linkage, so read returns 7.

p21.why: The static hidden in the second unit is private to that unit, so the external hidden that main calls has no definition.

p22.why: An earlier extern declaration keeps the const variable external, so the second unit reads 5.

p23.why: A const member cannot be mutable.

p24.why: The block extern refers to the namespace-scope shared, which is 5.

p25.why: A static declaration of g follows one with external linkage.

p26.why: static and extern are two storage classes.

p27.why: The header shared-limit.h is missing from the batch directory, so as given the include fails; assuming it declares one_limit external (extern or inline const), each_limit plain const, and far_limit extern const, the checks pass.

p28.why: The block extern behind a hiding local: EDG 7.0 rejects it, while Clang and GCC accept and read the static shared, so the program runs (Q-0105).

p29.why: Two units define the same non-inline function.

p30.why: A parameter must not have a storage class.

p31.why: The initializer of the block static calls get again while that initialization is still running.

p32.why: Static storage starts at zero, so every value is zero or null.

p33.why: A block extern follows a local variable of the same name in the same block.

p34.why: The two declarations of u disagree on thread_local.

p35.why: The block static is not initialized until control reaches it, so inits is 0 and then 1.

p36.why: A parameter must not have a storage class.

p37.why: A namespace-scope variable cannot be mutable.

p38.why: The namespace-scope anonymous union is static, so its member a is usable.

p39.why: The declarations of t disagree on thread_local.

p40.why: register is not a storage class.

p41.why: declared_only is called but no unit defines it.

p42.why: Each unit has its own static value and helper, so the values are 1, 10, 2, 20.

p43.why: The later extern x and the later f without a storage class keep internal linkage, so they differ from the external x and f of the second unit.

p44.why: A namespace-scope anonymous union must be static.

p45.why: extern with an initializer at namespace scope is a definition, so the second unit reads 42.

p46.why: The inline variable and function defined in both units are one entity with one address.

p47.why: The block function declaration and block extern refer to the namespace-scope entities defined in the second unit.

p48.why: The anonymous union in an unnamed namespace is not static; GCC and EDG reject it and Clang accepts it (Q-0045).

p49.why: A declaration that only defines a class must not have a storage class; Clang's pedantic warning becomes an error.

p50.why: The block static is initialized once to 10, then incremented to 11, 12, 13.

p51.why: A block-scope variable cannot be mutable.

p52.why: Declarations the program does not use need no definition.

p53.why: shared has external linkage, so both units see the one object holding 7.

p54.why: const and constexpr namespace-scope variables have internal linkage, so each unit has its own.

p55.why: A function must not be declared static in a block.

p56.why: A block extern declaration must not have an initializer.

p57.why: Names in an unnamed namespace are private to their unit, so each unit has its own value and helper.
